title: Item 9 Calibration — Stage B deterministic calibration engine
description: Implement the deterministic Item 9 Stage B calibration engine. The engine binds canonical explicit telemetry to Task Contracts, groups primary samples by LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, validates provenance/integrity/task binding/token budget/calibration eligibility, fails closed on missing or insufficient evidence, and emits no numeric quantiles until a conservative per-risk operational sample floor is met. It does not modify budgets or governance policy.

why_medium: This code becomes governance-supporting calibration logic used to interpret canonical telemetry.
A defect could produce misleading calibration statistics even though the stage cannot mutate policy or production business state.
The implementation is additive and isolated to multi-agent governance scripts/tests/docs.
why_not_high: No payment, pricing, inventory, authentication, authorization, migration, database, production runtime, GitHub ruleset, workflow, Human Gate, Security Gate, or merge-policy behavior is changed.
The engine explicitly sets policy_mutation_allowed=false and Stage C remains the only recommendation stage.

dependencies.name: Item 9 Stage A evidence and sample sufficiency baseline

lock.rule: No conflicting writer may mutate these paths until the Stage B PR is merged or aborted.

sample_sufficiency_rule.basis: Conservative operational floor only; not a claim of inferential statistical confidence. It prevents a single pilot or a tiny anecdotal sample from enabling P50/P75/P90 output. Stage C may use the output only as evidence and still cannot directly mutate policy.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Stage B is MEDIUM and requires exact-artifact Review PASS plus ACTIVE lock evidence. Security and Project Owner Human Gate are not required unless deterministic risk escalates.

acceptance_criteria.description: Engine groups calibration evidence independently into LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH using the bound Task Contract risk.

Only telemetry loaded from canonical .eqcofe/telemetry/<task_id>.json via verified readback may enter the calibration engine; invalid JSON, invalid provenance, task mismatch and tampered aggregates fail closed.

A missing canonical telemetry file is converted only to explicit MISSING_TELEMETRY evidence; malformed task IDs and every non-ENOENT read failure propagate as blockers rather than being treated as missing.
Task ID and token budget must match the bound Task Contract; mismatch fails closed.
Only MERGED and non-human-rejected records are primary samples; human-rejected or non-merged records remain visible but excluded.
Missing telemetry is represented as missing evidence and is never converted into zero usage.
Fewer than 10 primary samples in a risk class returns INSUFFICIENT_CANONICAL_TELEMETRY and emits no P50/P75/P90.
At 10 or more primary samples, deterministic nearest-rank token quantiles may be emitted for that class without changing any budget or policy.
Duplicate task IDs cannot inflate sample count and tampered aggregates or invalid provenance fail closed.
Existing wildcard multi-agent tests include Stage B with no package.json or workflow mutation; full canonical verification must remain green.
PR diff is limited to the five declared write-scope files and Stage B makes no recommendation or policy mutation.
Protected merge and exact-SHA post-merge canonical plus Phase A verification must pass before Stage B is canonically complete.

canonical_loading_rule.rule: Calibration statistics may only be produced from records loaded through canonical telemetry readback. In-memory records can be integrity-validated for unit-level checks but are not a canonical calibration source.
